intro: Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honour all of them. Today's roll was seed 2548416680. Here is each roll and what became of it.

rolls.became: TONIGHT'S SKY, the tape in the planetarium's VCR. The old star projector broke 35 years ago, so every night since, the dome has shown a video of the sky. The same video. The tape has watched its own Orion about 12,000 times. Its eyes are its reels, and they're half shut.
A tape is a long ribbon, and ribbon weaves: the tape unspools a bit of itself and weaves star frames, like the folded paper stars people hang in windows. Then it needs something to fill them with.

It fills them with TV static. Tune an old TV to nothing and roughly one speck of the snow in a hundred is the afterglow of the Big Bang, which makes it real starlight, just very old. So you hold to pour static into the star and let go at the line: on the line it counts double, too late and it spills.
The tape wants out, into a field, to see one sky that isn't a rerun.

Bylaw 1: the dome shows a sky every night. The Board will only retire a tape once its replacement is on file: Form F-88, Replacement of a Sky, all 88 constellations. So the tape has to build a sky that runs itself, and every trick on the way there is another form.
Florence, the Board's rubber stamp, who lives in the in-tray on the console and stamps every form. She'd like you to know she isn't the bad guy. She is a stamp.

rolls.value: a tech tree with exclusive choices
rolls.became: The Board's forms. Each form has two boxes, and Section 9 says one box per form: tick Steady Hand and Big Spout is VOID, take the Rewinders and you'll never get the Looms. Florence stamps the other box VOID, very gently.

rolls.value: a production chain on a small belt grid you lay out
rolls.became: Form F-7, the Permit to Run Tape Across a Walkway, opens the booth floor. You lay the tape from the VCR to the hatch up to the dome, and the static runs along it: TVs add static, Rewinders play it twice, funnels pour it into stars, and whatever gets past the last funnel reaches your hand-pour spout. The floor is small, so the order along the tape is the whole puzzle.

rolls.value: stacked currencies (A makes B, B makes C)
rolls.became: Static makes stars, and stars get strung into constellations. Static buys the silly things and a finer weave; stars buy the machines and pay Florence's filing fees; constellations are what the Board is counting.

rolls.value: slow things that ripen in real minutes
rolls.became: A strung constellation hangs on a hook in the dome and takes real minutes to come out, the way stars do at dusk: the static has to settle before the shape clears. It keeps settling while you're away, so you come back to find Orion done.
88 constellations, from little Triangulum to Orion, over several evenings. Time away counts: the TVs keep hissing at a quarter speed and dusk keeps coming.
Specks of static. A star takes a hundred, and by the end the TVs are hissing hundreds of billions of them into the booth.

Washes of indigo and teal for the night, citrus yellow for the stars, lime and green ink, everything painted with soft bled edges on paper. The headings are in marker, like a label somebody wrote on a tape.

Late-night VHS synthwave built only from whole steps: augmented chords that never quite resolve, so the music floats like a dome slowly turning. It thickens as the sky fills, and every pour, chime and stamp is on the same scale.

The tape runs an unlicensed after-hours show on the planetarium PA. Once you buy the Request Line, the callers start ringing in: the seats, a packet of astronaut ice cream from the gift shop, the old projector, the TVs (in TV), and eventually Florence.
No calendar nod today. Lacaille, who named a constellation after an air pump in the 1750s, gets a few shout-outs as a fellow sufferer of paperwork.

Everyone who called the Request Line wanted to know where the tape was going and whether they could come. When F-88 is stamped and the tape tries to slip out the fire door quietly, they all come along: TVs, funnels, the seats, the ice cream, the old projector, and Florence.

The send-off becomes a parade of everything you bought, marching out of the booth into the real night. The dome keeps showing its woven sky every night, just as Bylaw 1 says, to nobody, because they're all out in a field looking up.

outro: None of this was planned as one idea. It's a dozen dice, one true fact about TV static, and a lot of forms.
